head_coach_since: 2026-27 (hired Apr 30, 2026); previously Memphis Grizzlies 2019-20 to Mar 28, 2025
background: Wharton (Penn) graduate (born Sept 1984) who entered the NBA as a Spurs basketball-operations intern, won a D-League title as Austin Toros head coach (2012), then rose through Mike Budenholzer's staffs in Atlanta (2013-18) and Milwaukee (2018-19). Hired by Memphis at 34 in 2019 and became the franchise's winningest coach (250-214, .539) over six seasons: 56-26 and 51-31 in 2021-22 and 2022-23 (Coach of the Year runner-up 2022, one playoff series win), a 27-55 injury season in 2023-24, and 44-29 in 2024-25 when he was abruptly fired with nine games left after an in-season offensive overhaul (Noah LaRoche's five-out 'drive-kick-relocate' system, league-best 33.1% offensive rebounding rate) fractured staff alignment and de-emphasized Ja Morant. Milwaukee hired him on Apr 30, 2026 to replace Doc Rivers, with co-owner Jimmy Haslam citing his player-development record and defensive reputation; Darvin Ham remains on staff. Known for pace, offensive rebounding, egalitarian '.5 basketball' offense, an aggressive 'risk-reward' drop-based defense that funnels drivers to the rim protector, deep rotations and strong young-player development, but also for timeout gaffes and inconsistent playoff adjustments.
